Texto do anúncio: WARNING: I made a huge mistake after I bought the Complete Ethiopian Bible from FaithMade. I almost threw it away. Don't do what I almost did. Three weeks after I started reading it, I had it back in the box, ready to throw it in the trash. Not because it wasn't working. Because of what started happening after I opened it. Let me explain. I'm 54. I've been a Christian my entire life. Raised in church, never missed a Sunday, the whole thing. And somewhere along the way I had quietly accepted that a certain emptiness was just my normal. The prayers that felt like they hit the ceiling and stopped. The heaviness on my chest I could never explain. Reading scripture and still feeling lost, still feeling like I was on the outside of something everyone else seemed to feel. I'd asked God for answers for years and mostly heard silence. And like most women in my seat, I blamed myself. Figured I wasn't faithful enough. Not good enough. Not chosen the way other people were. Then one night I went down an internet rabbit hole and found out the Bible I'd been reading my whole life was missing twenty-two books. And that one nation had kept all eighty-eight of them for more than seventeen hundred years. That's when I found the Complete Ethiopian Bible from FaithMade. The full canon, eighty-eight books, in English. With the strange-sounding titles I'd never heard in any church I'd ever sat in. Enoch. Jubilees. Meqabyan. It seemed like a conspiracy. Like something a stranger in a comment section would push on you. But thousands of Christians were describing the same thing in the reviews, and I couldn't shake it. So I bought it. ======== My First Mistake I didn't tell a soul. Not my husband. Not my pastor. Not the women in my Bible study. And I knew exactly why. Because I knew exactly what they'd say. They'd call it fringe. They'd call it a conspiracy. Somebody would say it sounds like a cult, that I was adding books to the Bible, that you can't just go reading whatever you find online and call it scripture. The pastor would give me that careful, concerned look. Half of them would quote me the verse about not adding to the word, the same verse I'd half-worried about myself. So I kept it in a drawer and read it alone, late, after the house was quiet. Like I was getting away with something. That part still bothers me. That a believing woman felt like she had to hide reading more of the word. By the second week, something strange started happening. I read the Book of Enoch first. And the heaviness I'd carried for years, the low dread sitting behind everything, started to loosen. Not all at once. Just a little less every night. I told myself it was a coincidence. ======== The Real Thing Started in Week Three I woke up at three in the morning the way I always did, with that nameless fear pressing down on me. Normally I'd lie there and wait it out for an hour. White-knuckle it until the sun came up. But this time I prayed. And for the first time in longer than I can remember, it didn't feel like the words were bouncing back at me. It felt like they landed. Like I was covered. The dread that had sat on my chest for years. Nothing. It faded before it even took hold, and I rolled over and slept. ======== Here's Where I Almost Made My Biggest Mistake I nearly stopped reading it. I nearly taped that box shut and threw it out. Why? Because that old voice got loud. The one that said this was too much, that real Christians don't go chasing buried books, that I was wandering somewhere I'd regret. So let me say the thing I wish someone had said to me first, because I know it's the exact thing stopping you. This does not replace your King James. I'm not telling you the Bible you grew up with is wrong. I'm not telling you to throw it out. I still read mine every single morning. I didn't trade one Bible for another. This isn't a different Bible. It's the rest of it. It's the twenty-two books that were taken out, handed back to you, sitting next to the sixty-six you already trust. More scripture, not other scripture. The early church read all of it. They didn't see two Bibles. They saw one, whole. Once I understood that, the fear went quiet. I wasn't replacing the word. I was finally reading the parts of it that had been kept from me. Women like us have been conditioned to believe the power the Bible actually talks about was meant for other people. For the apostles, for the saints, for somebody holier than us. That feeling nothing was just the honest Christian life and anything more was suspicious. I almost threw all of it away because feeling that strong felt like a trick. ======== What's Actually Inside These Pages So I finally sat down and studied what was in this Bible that the one I grew up with didn't have. Here's what I found. ✅ The Book of Enoch: the map of the unseen world. The watchers, the fallen ones, the heavens laid out level by level, named and ordered. And here's the part that stopped me cold. The apostle Jude quotes this exact book in the New Testament. "Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied." It's sitting in your King James right now, quoting a book your King James leaves out. ✅ The Book of Jubilees: the history underneath Genesis. The timeline, the watchers' rebellion, the names and the origins that the trimmed version only hints at and never explains. ✅ The Book of the Covenant: the terms the early church understood that most believers today have never read a page of. ✅ The Ascension of Isaiah: the prophet carried up through the heavens, an account that lines up with what Enoch wrote, by a different man, centuries apart. ✅ Meqabyan (1, 2, 3): the Ethiopian books of the Maccabees. The faith-under-siege books, written by the people who actually held the line while empires fell around them. ✅ The prayers, the names of the spirits, and the angels assigned to your own household: the part the early believers used and the rest of the world had taken out of its hands. This wasn't just another Bible with a nicer cover. It was the complete word, the way the early church actually carried it, before sixty-six books got handed out as if that was everything God ever said. ======== And the Book Itself This is the other thing I wasn't expecting. The print is big. Large, clean, easy on the eyes. Not the cramped onionskin micro-text you squint at in most Bibles. You can actually sit and read it for an hour without a headache, and my mother can read it without reaching for her glasses. The translation isn't watered down. Nothing softened to make it more comfortable. Nothing smoothed over to avoid offending anyone. The hard parts are left hard, in plain English you can understand, the way they were actually written. And it's built like something you keep. A real book, a real binding, the kind of thing you hand to your daughter one day, not a flimsy paperback that falls apart in a year. ======== The Side Effect Nobody Warns You About About a month in, my husband said something I haven't stopped thinking about. "You pray different now." I asked him what he meant. He said it used to sound like I was asking permission. Now it sounds like I know who I'm talking to. I hadn't realized how much that quiet dread had been running my life. How much of me had gone silent over the years. How long I'd been a believer who was secretly scared. This Bible didn't just give me more to read. It gave me back something I thought wasn't meant for someone like me. ======== Why Most "Solutions" Make It Worse Before this, I'd tried everything to feel something again. ❌ The cheap Ethiopian Bibles on Amazon. Half the books quietly missing, translations softened past recognition, review after review of believers warning it wasn't the real thing. I almost lost real money on a counterfeit. ❌ Western study guides. They explain around the missing books instead of just handing them to you. A tour of the locked room instead of the key. ❌ Another devotional, another reading plan. More passes through the same sixty-six books, never the twenty-two that were taken out. ❌ Just praying harder. Willpower stacked on top of a Bible with the battle pages torn out of it. None of them touched the root. You were handed sixty-six books and told that was the whole story. The books that explain the unseen world, the ones the apostles were reading, were stripped out before the version you own ever reached your hands. ======== What I Wish Someone Had Told Me Sooner If you're living with: Prayers that feel like they stop at the ceiling and go no further. A heaviness you can't explain, or lying awake with a fear that has no name. Reading scripture for years and still feeling lost, still feeling outside of it. Blaming yourself. Thinking you're not faithful enough. Not good enough. Not chosen. Please don't waste years the way I did, believing that's just how faith feels and the silence is your fault. And please don't make my mistake of almost throwing it out the moment it finally starts working. You deserve to pray and feel it land. You deserve to read the whole story instead of half of it. You deserve to stop being a scared Christian and start being a covered one. And here's the part that made it easy for me to finally open it and stop second-guessing. FaithMade gives you a full 365-day money-back guarantee. A whole year to read it, sit with it, and decide. If nothing changes in you, you send it back and every cent comes home. I only wish I'd found it years ago. ======== Every Believer's Way In Is Different Some women need to start with Enoch and finally see the unseen world named and ordered. Some need Jubilees, to watch the history they half-knew finally click into place. And some need Meqabyan, the faith-under-siege books, to feel the backbone come back. There's no wrong door. The point is that for the first time the whole canon is in one place, in large readable English, the same eighty-eight books one nation guarded for more than seventeen hundred years. Sitting right next to the King James you already love, not in place of it. It comes with the complete eighty-eight book Ethiopian Bible fully translated into English, a two-hundred-plus-hour audiobook so the word stays with you while you drive and work and fall asleep, and the Master Apocrypha, the ancient texts the early church used that were stripped from the rest of the world, compiled in one place. Most places that sell anything close charge around three hundred dollars for the book alone. FaithMade has all of it for under fifty. Inventory is limited and each batch is printed and then gone, sometimes for weeks. If this page is still live, copies are still available. Open it. Read what an apostle quoted and a council buried. You've got a full year to decide, so there's nothing to lose. If nothing changes in you, send it back and every cent comes home. But once you read what was taken out, you're not going to want to. https://thefaithmade.com/pages/6-ways P.S. I don't make a cent from sharing this. I'm just a believer who spent years feeling nothing and finally got handed the books that were taken out, and I'd rather look crazy than watch another Christian go her whole life reading half the story. P.P.S. You get a full 365 days with it. A whole year to read every book they took out and decide for yourself. “The one place demons begged Jesus to avoid”
ver texto e fala completos
Texto do anúncio: The demons that met Jesus were not afraid to die. They were afraid of one place. Luke 8:31 reads: “And they begged Jesus repeatedly not to order them to go into the Abyss.” Those are demons speaking. A legion of them, standing in front of Jesus. And they are not begging for their lives. They are begging Him not to be sent to one place. The King James calls that place “the deep.” The Greek word is abyssos. The Abyss. So here is a question almost no Christian alive can answer. What is the Abyss? What is this one place, so terrible that a legion of demons would rather be sent anywhere else on earth than go there? And the second you start pulling on that thread, a bigger question opens up underneath it. Where did these things even come from in the first place? The answer to both questions was written down. Not in some fringe scroll that nobody trusted. The book that holds it was treated as scripture by the men who walked with Jesus. Jude, the brother of Jesus, quotes it by name and calls it prophecy. Jude 1:14, sitting in the New Testament right now. Peter points at it when he writes, in 1 Peter 3:19, that Jesus preached to spirits held in prison from the days of Noah. And centuries later, copies of it were pulled from the Dead Sea Scrolls, in the original ancient Aramaic, pre-Christian and authentic. Every mark of real scripture is on it. And it was still erased from your Bible. That book is the Book of Enoch. And it walks straight back into that scene and shows you what was really standing in front of Jesus. It tells you where they came from. Enoch chapter 6, verse 6. Two hundred angels called the Watchers came down in the days before the flood. They took human wives. Their children were the Nephilim, the giants. And when the flood destroyed the bodies of the Nephilim, their spirits did not die with their bodies. Enoch chapter 15, verse 8, says it in plain words. Those spirits became the evil spirits on the earth. They afflict, they oppress, they torment mankind, and they will keep doing it until the day of the final judgment. That is what a demon is. Enoch says it. Your Bible never does. The Book of Jubilees, chapter 10, verse 9, finishes the picture. After the flood these spirits went after humanity so fast that Noah cried out to God. God ordered them bound. But their prince begged that a tenth of them be left loose, to test and afflict mankind. And that tenth was permitted to remain. A remnant of them. Still loose on the earth. Right now. But none of that was what they feared most. That was the Abyss. Enoch does not leave it vague. In chapter 21, verse 7, he is taken there and shown it with his own eyes. He describes a place beyond the edge of everything, with no heaven above it and no ground beneath it. A pit of fire and darkness with no bottom to it. And chained inside it are the Watchers who fell. The two hundred who came down. The ones who fathered the Nephilim. Bound there in the dark, held for the day of judgment, waiting. And the ones who put them there were the archangels. Enoch chapter 10, verse 12, records the command. Michael. Raphael. The same seven that were cut out of your Bible. They are the ones who dragged the fallen down into that pit and sealed it over them. That is why a legion of demons dropped to the ground and begged. The Abyss is not just any prison. It is the prison where their own fathers are held in chains. It is the one place in all creation built for their kind. And they know that on the last day, it is where they are going. Now look at the scene again, and it stands all the way up. A man had been living out among the tombs. No chain could hold him. He cried out through the night, and not one person alive could help him. Then he saw Jesus. And the thing inside him knew Him on sight, before a single human in that story did, and screamed it out loud. Son of the Most High God. They knew Him because they had been at war with His side since before the flood. They had watched the archangels chain their fathers in the dark. And now the one Person with the authority to open that pit and throw them into it was standing on the shore, looking straight at them. That is why they were not begging for their lives. They already knew how this ends. They were begging for time. Anywhere but the Abyss. Not yet. And the Book of Enoch does not just expose the enemy. It shows you who fights for you. Your Bible names two angels. Michael and Gabriel. Enoch chapter 20 names all seven archangels and what each one is assigned to do. The same archangels who chained the Watchers in the Abyss in the first place. The Book of Tobit shows one of them, the angel Raphael, walking beside a young man, guarding him, and in chapter 8, verse 3, driving a demon off him. These were the names the early church prayed with. The West cut them out and told believers to make peace with vagueness. And they cut out something heavier still. What Jesus Himself said about all of this. Your own Bible tells you that after He rose from the dead, He did not leave right away. He stayed and taught for forty more days. Acts 1:3. Forty days of teaching from the risen Christ. And your Bible records almost none of what He said in them. But it survived. It is called the Book of the Covenant. In those pages the risen Jesus does not speak as a gentle teacher. He speaks as the King of heaven and earth. He warns His followers what is coming. He teaches them about the powers of darkness, and how a believer is meant to stand against them. The very instructions the West left on the floor. And in that same teaching, He said something about authority that the powerful have never wanted repeated. He warned that a day would come when people would seize His name and use it for their own gain. They would shout it in the streets. They would build kingdoms and cathedrals in it. They would wear His name like a badge while their hearts stayed far from Him. Your own Bible says the same thing, in Matthew 15:8. These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me. And Jesus said plainly that He does not hand His authority to them. Not to the loud. Not to the powerful. Not to the ones who wear His name for profit. He trusts it to one kind of person only. The one who believes in Him deep in their heart. The humble. The overlooked. The ones the world never bothers to notice. Because real authority was never a title or a robe. It was a fire, and it only burns in a believer who actually knows what he is carrying. The early church knew it. They walked into rooms and sickness fled. They spoke His name over a tormented man and the thing inside him came out screaming. In Luke 10:19 Jesus had told them plainly, I have given you authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. They did not read that as poetry. They used it. And it worked, because they held the complete word, with the whole map of the enemy open in their hands. Then the books were cut. And the church slowly forgot the authority it once carried. It kept the buildings and lost the fire. Here is the part that should make every believer sit up. The bloodline the Watchers left behind did not drown in the flood. Enoch already told you what happened to it. The spirits of the dead Nephilim are still here, still roaming, still doing the one thing Enoch said they would do. They afflict. They oppress. They torment. They are the reason for the heaviness that will not lift. The dread that has no cause. The war going on around a believer that no one else can see. It is not new and it is not random. It is the same enemy that has been working since before the flood, and it has never once stopped. And it has help. The people who long ago made their peace with that darkness, who traded the truth for power and built the kingdoms of this world on it, are still here too. They sit on thrones and behind pulpits. They shout His name the loudest of anyone. They keep the world loud and distracted and unarmed. And yet they hold no authority over the darkness at all, because they never truly believed in the first place. The authority they perform for the cameras was never theirs to hold. It was always meant for the believer who reads the whole word and believes it down in his bones. But the believers that authority was meant for are the very ones who were robbed of it. They lie awake at three in the morning, certain the room has gone wrong, certain they are not alone in it. And everyone around them has an easy answer for it. It is the job. It is the stress. It is just the weight of ordinary life catching up. Sleep it off. But it gets worse the harder they try to get close to God. Every time they decide to pray more, read more, actually walk with Him, something pushes back. The dreams get darker. The pressure gets heavier. The closer they move toward the light, the deeper something drags them the other way. They carry it to the people who are supposed to help, and they are told their faith is weak, or it is only anxiety, take something for it. So they start to wonder if they are simply broken. Or worse, if they are cursed. Their prayers feel like they hit the ceiling and slide back down, like they are talking to no one. Nobody can tell them what they are actually dealing with. The book that was cut out of their Bible can. What has been finding them in the dark is not weak faith and it is not imagination. It is real. It has a name. It has an origin. It has an expiration date and a prison already built for it. And every word of it was written down in a book that was taken out of the Bible before they were ever born. Which is the question that should stop every Christian cold. If Jude quoted Enoch as scripture, if Jesus spoke as though His followers had read it, if the answer to what demons are and where they are held was sitting right there, how did it ever get out of your Bible. Somebody made that decision. The original King James Bible, printed in 1611, had 80 books. Not 66. The extra books sat in the middle of it for over two hundred years. Then in 1826 a British printing society made a business decision. Cut the extra books, or lose their funding. They cut them. To save on ink. And in 1947 a shepherd boy threw a rock into a cave and found the oldest Bible manuscripts on earth. The Dead Sea Scrolls. Among them, copies of the Book of Enoch that had sat there since before Christ walked. They did not match the 66-book Protestant Bible. They matched the Ethiopian one. One country never made the cut. The first Christian nation on earth. The only nation in Africa that never bowed to a colonial ruler. The country that still claims to guard the Ark of the Covenant in a chapel in Axum. Ethiopia kept the Book of Enoch. Kept Jubilees. Kept the full 88 books while the West trimmed the rest down to what was cheap to print. Ethiopia did not add books. Everyone else removed them. Say it plainly, because the comments will twist it. This is not a claim that your Bible is wrong. Every word in it is true and it is still His. The complete Bible does not change a single book you already own. It gives back the 22 that were taken out. The 22 that happen to hold the entire map of what has been fighting you in the dark. This is not replacement. This is restoration. And that map is what finally lets a believer sleep through the night. When you finally know what you are up against, and Who is standing between you and it, the fear breaks. You stop lying there as a victim of something you cannot name. Faith comes from hearing the word of God. They cut that hearing in half, and then the church told you the fear was your fault. It was never your fault. You were sent into a real fight with half the map missing. The heaviness may still visit some nights. The difference is you know exactly what it is now. Where it came from. Whose chains it is running out of time before it returns to. And Who holds the key to that prison. You stop being a scared Christian. You become a Christian who has finally read the whole book. Now here is the hard part. And this is where I have to tell you how I found all of this out. I went looking for a real, complete Ethiopian Bible myself. And I learned fast how hard that is. Since Enoch started trending, Amazon filled up with counterfeits that call themselves complete and quietly leave books out. Chapters missing. Passages softened. I bought one, and then another, and then another. I lost almost four hundred dollars before I realized every copy I could get my hands on was still censored. I had nearly given up. Then I found a small group of believers in America who could not let it go either. They had done the thing nobody else was willing to do. They flew to Ethiopia. Straight to the source. The one place that never changed a word. And they brought the complete Bible home in English. Word for word. Nothing softened. Nothing left out. They call it Faith Made. The full 88 books. The Book of Enoch. The Book of Jubilees. The Wisdom of Solomon. And every other ancient scripture the Western church carved away. Because most Christians have never seen these books in their lives, every printed copy ships with a free audiobook that walks through every one of them. By the time you finish, you will understand what you are fighting, and Who fights for you, better than most pastors who have preached for thirty years. Most stores that sell the Ethiopian Bible charge close to a hundred dollars. Faith Made put the whole thing together for under fifty. And there is no risk in seeing it for yourself. They give you 30 days. 30 days to read what the Abyss actually is. 30 days to finally know the name of the thing that has been finding people in the dark. And if it does not change the way you pray, the way you read your Bible, or the way you sleep at night, send it back for every penny returned. No questions asked. Faith Made prints in batches. When a batch sells out it can be weeks or months before the next one is ready. So if the link below still works, it is still available. The demons knew exactly what they were afraid of. It is time you did too. Click the link below before this batch is gone. https://thefaithmade.com/pages/last-days P.S. I gave this Bible to a woman who had been waking at night the same way. She called me two days later. For the first time in years, she said, the room felt quiet. Not because the enemy left. Because she finally knew what it was, and Who already won. P.P.S. If the link is still up, they still have copies. https://thefaithmade.com/pages/last-days

He describes a place beyond the edge of everything, with no heaven above it and no ground beneath it. A pit of fire and darkness with no bottom to it. And chained inside it are the Watchers who fell. The two hundred who came down. The ones who fathered the Nephilim. Bound there in the dark, held for the day of judgment, waiting. And the ones who put them there were the archangels. Enoch chapter 10, verse 12, records the command. Michael. Raphael. The same seven that were cut out of your Bible. They are the ones who dragged the fallen down into that pit and sealed it over them. That is why a legion of demons dropped to the ground and begged. The Abyss is not just any prison. It is the prison where their own fathers are held in chains. It is the one place in all creation built for their kind. And they know that on the last day, it is where they are going. Now look at the scene again, and it stands all the way up. A man had been living out among the tombs. No chain could hold him. He cried out through the night, and not one person alive could help him. Then he saw Jesus. And the thing inside him knew Him on sight, before a single human in that story did, and screamed it out loud. Son of the Most High God. They knew Him because they had been at war with His side since before the flood. They had watched the archangels chain their fathers in the dark. And now the one Person with the authority to open that pit and throw them into it was standing on the shore, looking straight at them. That is why they were not begging for their lives. They already knew how this ends. They were begging for time. Anywhere but the Abyss. Not yet. And the Book of Enoch does not just expose the enemy. It shows you who fights for you. Your Bible names two angels. Michael and Gabriel. Enoch chapter 20 names all seven archangels and what each one is assigned to do. The same archangels who chained the Watchers in the Abyss in the first place. The Book of Tobit shows one of them, the angel Raphael, walking beside a young man, guarding him, and in chapter 8, verse 3, driving a demon off him. These were the names the early church prayed with. The West cut them out and told believers to make peace with vagueness. And they cut out something heavier still. What Jesus Himself said about all of this. Your own Bible tells you that after He rose from the dead, He did not leave right away. He stayed and taught for forty more days. Acts 1:3. Forty days of teaching from the risen Christ. And your Bible records almost none of what He said in them. But it survived. It is called the Book of the Covenant. In those pages the risen Jesus does not speak as a gentle teacher. He speaks as the King of heaven and earth. He warns His followers what is coming. He teaches them about the powers of darkness, and how a believer is meant to stand against them. The very instructions the West left on the floor. And in that same teaching, He said something about authority that the powerful have never wanted repeated. He warned that a day would come when people would seize His name and use it for their own gain. They would shout it in the streets. They would build kingdoms and cathedrals in it. They would wear His name like a badge while their hearts stayed far from Him. Your own Bible says the same thing, in Matthew 15:8. These people honor me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me. And Jesus said plainly that He does not hand His authority to them. Not to the loud. Not to the powerful. Not to the ones who wear His name for profit. He trusts it to one kind of person only. The one who believes in Him deep in their heart. The humble. The overlooked. The ones the world never bothers to notice. Because real authority was never a title or a robe. It was a fire, and it only burns in a believer who actually knows what he is carrying. The early church knew it. They walked into rooms and sickness fled. They spoke His name over a tormented man and the thing inside him came out screaming. In Luke 10:19 Jesus had told them plainly, I have given you authority to trample on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy. They did not read that as poetry. They used it. And it worked, because they held the complete word, with the whole map of the enemy open in their hands. Then the books were cut. And the church slowly forgot the authority it once carried. It kept the buildings and lost the fire. Here is the part that should make every believer sit up. The bloodline the Watchers left behind did not drown in the flood. Enoch already told you what happened to it. The spirits of the dead Nephilim are still here, still roaming, still doing the one thing Enoch said they would do. They afflict. They oppress. They torment. They are the reason for the heaviness that will not lift. The dread that has no cause. The war going on around a believer that no one else can see. It is not new and it is not random. It is the same enemy that has been working since before the flood, and it has never once stopped. And it has help. The people who long ago made their peace with that darkness, who traded the truth for power and built the kingdoms of this world on it, are still here too. They sit on thrones and behind pulpits. They shout His name the loudest of anyone. They keep the world loud and distracted and unarmed. And yet they hold no authority over the darkness at all, because they never truly believed in the first place. The authority they perform for the cameras was never theirs to hold. It was always meant for the believer who reads the whole word and believes it down in his bones. But the believers that authority was meant for are the very ones who were robbed of it. They lie awake at three in the morning, certain the room has gone wrong, certain they are not alone in it. And everyone around them has an easy answer for it. It is the job. It is the stress. It is just the weight of ordinary life catching up. Sleep it off. But it gets worse the harder they try to get close to God. Every time they decide to pray more, read more, actually walk with Him, something pushes back. The dreams get darker. The pressure gets heavier. The closer they move toward the light, the deeper something drags them the other way. They carry it to the people who are supposed to help, and they are told their faith is weak, or it is only anxiety, take something for it. So they start to wonder if they are simply broken. Or worse, if they are cursed. Their prayers feel like they hit the ceiling and slide back down, like they are talking to no one. Nobody can tell them what they are actually dealing with. The book that was cut out of their Bible can. What has been finding them in the dark is not weak faith and it is not imagination. It is real. It has a name. It has an origin. It has an expiration date and a prison already built for it. And every word of it was written down in a book that was taken out of the Bible before they were ever born. Which is the question that should stop every Christian cold. If Jude quoted Enoch as scripture, if Jesus spoke as though His followers had read it, if the answer to what demons are and where they are held was sitting right there, how did it ever get out of your Bible. Somebody made that decision. The original King James Bible, printed in 1611, had 80 books. Not 66. The extra books sat in the middle of it for over two hundred years. Then in 1826 a British printing society made a business decision. Cut the extra books, or lose their funding. They cut them. To save on ink. And in 1947 a shepherd boy threw a rock into a cave and found the oldest Bible manuscripts on earth. The Dead Sea Scrolls. Among them, copies of the Book of Enoch that had sat there since before Christ walked. They did not match the 66-book Protestant Bible. They matched the Ethiopian one. One country never made the cut. The first Christian nation on earth. The only nation in Africa that never bowed to a colonial ruler. The country that still claims to guard the Ark of the Covenant in a chapel in Axum. Ethiopia kept the Book of Enoch. Kept Jubilees. Kept the full 88 books while the West trimmed the rest down to what was cheap to print. Ethiopia did not add books. Everyone else removed them. Say it plainly, because the comments will twist it. This is not a claim that your Bible is wrong. Every word in it is true and it is still His. The complete Bible does not change a single book you already own. It gives back the 22 that were taken out. The 22 that happen to hold the entire map of what has been fighting you in the dark. This is not replacement. This is restoration. And that map is what finally lets a believer sleep through the night. When you finally know what you are up against, and Who is standing between you and it, the fear breaks. You stop lying there as a victim of something you cannot name. Faith comes from hearing the word of God. They cut that hearing in half, and then the church told you the fear was your fault. It was never your fault. You were sent into a real fight with half the map missing. The heaviness may still visit some nights. The difference is you know exactly what it is now. Where it came from. Whose chains it is running out of time before it returns to. And Who holds the key to that prison. You stop being a scared Christian. You become a Christian who has finally read the whole book. Now here is the hard part. And this is where I have to tell you how I found all of this out. I went looking for a real, complete Ethiopian Bible myself. And I learned fast how hard that is. Since Enoch started trending, Amazon filled up with counterfeits that call themselves complete and quietly leave books out. Chapters missing. Passages softened. I bought one, and then another, and then another. I lost almost four hundred dollars before I realized every copy I could get my hands on was still censored. I had nearly given up. Then I found a small group of believers in America who could not let it go either. They had done the thing nobody else was willing to do. They flew to Ethiopia. Straight to the source. The one place that never changed a word. And they brought the complete Bible home in English. Word for word. Nothing softened. Nothing left out. They call it Faith Made. The full 88 books. The Book of Enoch. The Book of Jubilees. The Wisdom of Solomon. And every other ancient scripture the Western church carved away. Because most Christians have never seen these books in their lives, every printed copy ships with a free audiobook that walks through every one of them. By the time you finish, you will understand what you are fighting, and Who fights for you, better than most pastors who have preached for thirty years. Most stores that sell the Ethiopian Bible charge close to a hundred dollars. Faith Made put the whole thing together for under fifty. And there is no risk in seeing it for yourself. They give you 30 days. 30 days to read what the Abyss actually is. 30 days to finally know the name of the thing that has been finding people in the dark. And if it does not change the way you pray, the way you read your Bible, or the way you sleep at night, send it back for every penny returned. No questions asked. Faith Made prints in batches. When a batch sells out it can be weeks or months before the next one is ready. So if the link below still works, it is still available. The demons knew exactly what they were afraid of. It is time you did too. Click the link below before this batch is gone. https://thefaithmade.com/pages/6-ways P.S. I gave this Bible to a woman who had been waking at night the same way. She called me two days later. For the first time in years, she said, the room felt quiet. Not because the enemy left. Because she finally knew what it was, and Who already won. P.P.S. Texto do anúncio: Everyone thinks Noah took 2 of every animal. He only took 2 of the ones the Nephilim had touched. Genesis 6:4 says the Nephilim were on the earth in the days of Noah, and also afterward. Before the flood, the earth had become hell. Genesis says the whole earth was filled with violence, and the blood of the innocent soaked so deep into the ground that it cried out to God. The wickedness sank into the soil until the earth itself was sick. It corrupted the trees, it turned the animals into beasts, and it poisoned every living thing that walked or grew on the face of the earth. So what made the world so wicked that God had to drown it? It started with a group of angels called the Watchers. They looked down from heaven, lusted after the daughters of men, and gave up eternity to have them. And when those angels bred with human women, they created something that was never meant to exist. The Nephilim. But the Watchers did something even worse. The Book of Enoch records that they handed their children forbidden knowledge. They had stood in the presence of God, they knew the secrets of heaven, how God formed every living thing and how the unseen world moves behind the one we see. That knowledge was never meant to leave heaven, but the Watchers dragged it down to earth, twisted it, and taught their children how to rule with it. They taught men warfare, sorcery, astrology and blood magic. The Nephilim were born with their fathers’ hatred for God. They hunted people, devoured them and drank their blood, chasing the power the forbidden knowledge had promised them. And when that wasn’t enough, they turned on everything else God had made. The cattle, the birds, every creature that crawled on the ground, they twisted what God had written into them until they became things God never made. Trees grew to monstrous size. Animals stopped looking like animals and turned into beasts. And men were mixed with the Nephilim bloodline, creating abominations God never created. Genesis 6:6 says it grieved God to His heart that He had made man. Not only because men sinned, but because what He made was no longer what He made. Human blood was no longer fully human, and men no longer carried the image of God. The flood wasn’t just punishment. It was God erasing what the Nephilim corrupted, so humanity could be human again. But before the rain came, God gave Noah the strangest command in all of scripture. He told Noah to bring 7 pairs of every clean animal, and 1 pair of every unclean animal, onto the ark. It’s right there in Genesis 7:2. Unclean meant corrupted, touched by what the Nephilim had done to God’s creation. And God told Noah to bring them on board anyway. Noah didn’t just carry God’s creation through the flood. He carried the Nephilim’s too. That’s how the bloodline survived. Within a few generations the giants were back, the spies Moses sent into the promised land came home saying they looked like grasshoppers next to them, and David stood in front of one of them, a giant named Goliath who defied the armies of the living God. But the bloodline wasn’t the most dangerous thing that survived the flood. The water drowned the bodies of the Nephilim, but it couldn’t drown what was inside them. The Book of Enoch says that when the giants died, their spirits came out of their bodies as evil spirits. Heaven was never made for them, so they stayed here on the earth, restless and hungry, looking for someone to torment. And the first family they came after was Noah’s. But Noah was an old man by then. He had built the ark with his own hands, listened to the screaming outside the door as the water rose, and carried his sons and their wives through the end of the world. And when the ground finally dried and his sons had children of their own, he watched those spirits come for his grandchildren. The Book of Jubilees says they began leading Noah’s grandchildren astray, to make them stumble and to destroy them. The first children born into the world God had just washed clean were being dragged into the same darkness He had just drowned. Noah fell before God and begged Him. He reminded God what the Watchers, the fathers of these spirits, had done in his day, and he cried out for God not to let wicked spirits rule over his grandchildren and wipe them off the earth. And God heard him. He commanded His angels to bind every one of those spirits. But the chief of the spirits begged God to leave him some, and God let 1 out of every 10 stay on the earth. That 1 in 10 never left. So God sent His angels to Noah to teach him how to stand against them. They showed Noah how the spirits deceive, and how to heal the sickness they bring with what God planted in the earth. And Noah wrote every word down in a book, so his grandchildren, and their grandchildren after them, would never stand defenseless again. But here’s what almost nobody has ever told you. Every family alive today comes from Noah’s grandchildren. Genesis 9:19 says that from Noah’s 3 sons the whole earth was filled. Then Genesis 10 names their children one by one, and closes by saying that from these families the nations were divided in the earth after the flood. Every nation, every family line, every one of us traces back to the grandchildren Noah prayed over. That means you are Noah’s grandchild. The same spirits that came for his family are still here, and they’re coming for you. But they don’t start with the people who are asleep. They start with the ones who see it coming. You’ve felt it. The closer you get to God, the harder something pushes back. The heaviness that settles over the house the moment you sit down to pray. The thoughts that come out of nowhere in the middle of the night. The prayers you pour your whole heart into that seem to hit the ceiling and fall right back down. And you look around at a world that laughs at the Bible like it’s a children’s story, the same way they laughed at Noah while he built the ark, and every year you feel a little more alone in your faith. Noah felt that too. He preached while he built, and they mocked him right up until the day the water came. When God shut the door, only 8 people were inside. You were never crazy for seeing what you see, and it was never that you didn’t pray hard enough. You were standing against the 1 in 10 without the book God gave Noah to stand with. But for centuries, the early church read these books as scripture. Jesus told His disciples the end would look just like the days of Noah. His own brother Jude quotes the Book of Enoch word for word in the New Testament. And Peter writes about the spirits in prison who disobeyed in the days of Noah. But slowly, church leaders began calling these books dangerous. One council at a time, they were pulled out, burned, and called heretical for exposing too much. And the Bible got smaller and smaller, until most believers grew up never knowing the prayer Noah prayed over them. That’s why so many passages in your Bible point to something that isn’t there. And none of it was an accident. Because a believer who knows how the enemy works, who prays what Noah prayed, and who can see the attack coming before it reaches the house is a believer the enemy can’t touch. So those books were stripped out, and God’s people were left fighting a war they were never allowed to understand. But God never loses. And the way He protected Noah’s book was hidden in Genesis the whole time. Open your Bible to Genesis 10. Noah’s son Ham had a son named Cush. Cush was Noah’s grandson, one of the very grandchildren Noah fell on his face and prayed over. Now turn back to Genesis 2:13 in your King James. The river that flowed out of Eden ran around the whole land of Ethiopia. In the Hebrew, that land is called Cush. Every time your King James Old Testament says Ethiopia, the word underneath it is Cush, the land of Noah’s grandson. And once you see it, you see it everywhere. Moses married a woman of Cush, and when his own brother and sister turned on him for it, God Himself defended him. When Jeremiah was thrown into a pit of mud to die, the man who pulled him out was from Cush. The Psalms promise that Ethiopia will soon stretch out her hands to God. And in Acts 8, God sent His messenger running down a desert road to one man, an Ethiopian riding home reading the prophet Isaiah. Ethiopia was never a random nation. It’s the land of Noah’s grandson, and God wove it through your Bible from the Garden of Eden to the Book of Acts. So when the rest of the world cut Noah’s story out of its Bibles, the land of Cush kept it. The only complete copies of the Book of Enoch and the Book of Jubilees left anywhere on earth survived in Ethiopia, written in Ethiopia’s ancient language. Everywhere else they were burned, banned or lost. Think about what that means. The prayer Noah prayed to protect his grandchildren was kept safe for thousands of years by the family of the grandchild it protected. And because you are Noah’s grandchild too, that prayer was prayed over you. Ethiopia is the only nation in Africa that was never colonized. No empire ever ruled it, so no one could ever reach inside their churches and cut a single page from their Bible. That’s why Ethiopia has the biggest Bible in the world, with 88 books. The same 66 books you were given, plus the 22 the rest of the world took out. They even kept God’s name. Where your Bible says Lord, theirs says Yahweh. The Book of Enoch is there, with the full story of the Watchers and what happened to the spirits of their children. The Book of Jubilees is there, with the prayer Noah prayed over his grandchildren, the 1 in 10 that were left behind, and what God’s angels taught Noah to do about them. Enoch names the archangels who stand before God and what each one watches over, and he wrote his warnings for a generation far in the future, the generation that would see the end. And that’s the generation Jesus said would look just like the days of Noah. A small group of believers set out to put that Bible back in the hands of every family. They gave themselves a name, The Faith Made, and they had one mission, to put all 88 books Ethiopia kept into one Bible, in plain English, with nothing left out. Over 200,000 Christians are reading it now, and they’re sharing testimony after testimony of what God is doing in their homes. Some of them write in tears that the heaviness finally left the house, that their prayers finally feel like they reach God, and that for the first time in their lives the Bible makes sense from Genesis to Revelation. But The Faith Made is small. They print in batches, and when a batch sells out it can be weeks before the next one. If the link below still works, they still have copies. And there’s no risk in trying it. The Faith Made gives you a full 365 day guarantee. That’s a full year to pray what Noah prayed over his grandchildren, to read what the angels taught him, and to read the whole story the enemy tried to bury. And if it’s not what you expected, send it back for a full refund, no questions asked. God shut the door of the ark to carry Noah’s family through the flood, and He carried Noah’s book through thousands of years in the land of Noah’s own grandson. Now it’s waiting for you, his grandchild. Get the complete Bible, the link is right below. 👉 https://thefaithmade.com/pages/the-22-books P.S. If you’re afraid these books go against the Bible you already have, they don’t. The 88 don’t contradict the 66, they complete them, and every book you already love is still there word for word. It’s printed on full 8.5 by 11 inch pages, so you’ll never have to squint at a single verse. 👉 Get your complete Bible here: https://thefaithmade.com/pages/the-22-books

Over 200,000 Christians are reading it now, and they’re sharing testimony after testimony of what God is doing in their homes.
